manifest.title: Max Independent Set Remains NP-hard when Excluding a Planar Induced Minor

inputs.abstract:
Maximum Independent Set is NP-hard on graphs excluding the $5\times5$ grid
as an induced minor. A polynomial-time reduction from Max Cut maps a graph
$F$ to a graph $G_F$ in this class such that
$\alpha(G_F)=\operatorname{MaxCut}(F)+2\sum_{uv\in E(F),\,u<v}(v-u)$.
Exclusion of the induced grid minor follows from an obstruction involving
an asteroidal triple of cycles.

This contradicts the polynomial-time conjecture of Dallard–Milanič–Štorgel
and its weighted induced-subgraph generalization unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$,
and the quasipolynomial-time conjecture of Gartland–Lokshtanov and Korhonen
unless $\mathrm{NP}\subseteq\mathrm{QP}$.

concepts.title: Asteroidal triples of cycles
concepts.description:
An asteroidal triple of cycles consists of three vertex-disjoint, pairwise
nonadjacent cycles such that every pair is joined by a path avoiding the
closed neighborhood of the third.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Paths

/-!
---
title: Asteroidal triples of cycles
type: definition
---
An asteroidal triple of cycles consists of three vertex-disjoint, pairwise
nonadjacent cycles such that every pair is joined by a path avoiding the
closed neighborhood of the third.
-/

namespace Lax762056.AsteroidalCycles

open SimpleGraph

def AvoidsClosedNeighborhood {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (S T : Set V) : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ T, x ≠ y ∧ ¬ G.Adj x y

def HasAsteroidalCycleTriple {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (base : Fin 3 → V) (cycle : ∀ i, Walk G (base i) (base i)),
    (∀ i, (cycle i).IsCycle) ∧
    (Pairwise fun i j => AvoidsClosedNeighborhood G
      {v | v ∈ (cycle i).support} {v | v ∈ (cycle j).support}) ∧
    (∀ i j k, i ≠ j → i ≠ k → j ≠ k →
      ∃ u ∈ (cycle i).support, ∃ v ∈ (cycle j).support,
        ∃ p : Path G u v, AvoidsClosedNeighborhood G
          {x | x ∈ p.val.support} {x | x ∈ (cycle k).support})

end Lax762056.AsteroidalCycles

concepts.title: Row and column graphs
concepts.description:
For a row set $R$ and $c$ columns, the graph has vertices
$(r,j,s)\in R\times\{0,\ldots,c-1\}\times\{0,1\}$. Each column induces a
complete bipartite graph between its two sides. Within a row, every vertex
is adjacent to both vertices in each consecutive column. There are no other
edges.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic

/-!
---
title: Row and column graphs
type: definition
---
For a row set $R$ and $c$ columns, the graph has vertices
$(r,j,s)\in R\times\{0,\ldots,c-1\}\times\{0,1\}$. Each column induces a
complete bipartite graph between its two sides. Within a row, every vertex
is adjacent to both vertices in each consecutive column. There are no other
edges.
-/

namespace Lax762056.ColumnGraph

open SimpleGraph

abbrev Vertex (R : Type*) (c : ℕ) := R × Fin c × Bool

def columnGraph (R : Type*) (c : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (Vertex R c) :=
  fromRel fun (row, column, side) (row', column', side') =>
    (column = column' ∧ side ≠ side') ∨
    (row = row' ∧ (column.val + 1 = column'.val ∨ column'.val + 1 = column.val))

end Lax762056.ColumnGraph

concepts.title: Asteroidal cycle triples obstruct induced minors
concepts.description:
No graph containing an asteroidal triple of cycles is an induced minor of
a row and column graph. The $5\times5$ grid contains such a triple.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax762056.AsteroidalCycles
import Lax762056.ColumnGraph
import Lax762056.Grid

/-!
---
title: Asteroidal cycle triples obstruct induced minors
type: lemma
---
No graph containing an asteroidal triple of cycles is an induced minor of
a row and column graph. The $5\times5$ grid contains such a triple.
-/

namespace Lax762056.CycleObstruction

open AsteroidalCycles ColumnGraph Grid InducedMinors

axiom asteroidalCycles_obstruction (R W : Type*) (c : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph W)
    (hH : HasAsteroidalCycleTriple H) :
  ¬ IsInducedMinor H (columnGraph R c)

axiom grid_five_has_asteroidalCycles : HasAsteroidalCycleTriple (squareGrid 5)

end Lax762056.CycleObstruction

statements.signature:
asteroidalCycles_obstruction : ∀ (R : Type u_1) (W : Type u_2) (c : Nat) (H : SimpleGraph W),
  Lax762056.AsteroidalCycles.HasAsteroidalCycleTriple H →
    Not (Lax762056.InducedMinors.IsInducedMinor H (Lax762056.ColumnGraph.columnGraph R c))

concepts.title: Binary encoding of graph decision instances
concepts.description:
An instance consists of a finite simple graph on $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and a
threshold $k$. Its encoding is $1^n0$, followed by the $n^2$ adjacency-matrix
bits in row order, followed by $1^k0$. Polynomial running time is measured
in the length of this word.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Clique
import Mathlib.Data.List.FinRange
import Lax434930.PolynomialTime

/-!
---
title: Binary encoding of graph decision instances
type: definition
---
An instance consists of a finite simple graph on $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and a
threshold $k$. Its encoding is $1^n0$, followed by the $n^2$ adjacency-matrix
bits in row order, followed by $1^k0$. Polynomial running time is measured
in the length of this word.
-/

namespace Lax762056.GraphEncoding

open List Turing Lax434930.PolynomialTime

structure Instance where
  order : ℕ
  graph : SimpleGraph (Fin order)
  threshold : ℕ

def unary (n : ℕ) : Word := replicate n true ++ [false]

noncomputable def encode (I : Instance) : Word := by
  classical
  exact unary I.order ++
    (finRange I.order).flatMap (fun u =>
      (finRange I.order).map (fun v => decide (I.graph.Adj u v))) ++
    unary I.threshold

def PolynomialTime (f : Instance → Instance) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (TM2ComputableInPolyTime encode encode f)

end Lax762056.GraphEncoding

concepts.title: Graph decision problems and NP-hardness
concepts.description:
Independent Set asks whether a graph has an independent set of size at least
$k$. Max Cut asks whether it has a cut with at least $k$ crossing edges.

A graph problem is NP-hard on a class $\mathcal C$ if every language in NP
has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to the problem whose output graph
always belongs to $\mathcal C$. Instances use the adjacency-matrix encoding.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax762056.MaxCut
import Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime

/-!
---
title: Graph decision problems and NP-hardness
type: definition
---
Independent Set asks whether a graph has an independent set of size at least
$k$. Max Cut asks whether it has a cut with at least $k$ crossing edges.

A graph problem is NP-hard on a class $\mathcal C$ if every language in NP
has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to the problem whose output graph
always belongs to $\mathcal C$. Instances use the adjacency-matrix encoding.
-/

namespace Lax762056.GraphProblems

open GraphEncoding MaxCut Turing
open Lax434930.PolynomialTime Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime

abbrev GraphClass := ∀ {n : ℕ}, SimpleGraph (Fin n) → Prop
abbrev DecisionProblem := Instance → Prop

def IndependentSet (I : Instance) : Prop := I.threshold ≤ I.graph.indepNum

def MaxCut (I : Instance) : Prop := I.threshold ≤ maxCut I.graph

def NPHard (problem : DecisionProblem) : Prop :=
  ∀ A : Language, A ∈ NP →
    ∃ f : Word → Instance,
      Nonempty (TM2ComputableInPolyTime id encode f) ∧
      ∀ x, x ∈ A ↔ problem (f x)

def NPHardOn (problem : DecisionProblem) (graphs : GraphClass) : Prop :=
  ∀ A : Language, A ∈ NP →
    ∃ f : Word → Instance,
      Nonempty (TM2ComputableInPolyTime id encode f) ∧
      ∀ x, graphs (f x).graph ∧ (x ∈ A ↔ problem (f x))

end Lax762056.GraphProblems

concepts.title: Excluded induced grid minors
concepts.description:
The $k\times k$ square grid is the Cartesian product of two $k$-vertex paths.
A graph excludes the induced grid of size $k$ if this square grid is not
an induced minor of the graph.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Hasse
import Lax762056.InducedMinors

/-!
---
title: Excluded induced grid minors
type: definition
---
The $k\times k$ square grid is the Cartesian product of two $k$-vertex paths.
A graph excludes the induced grid of size $k$ if this square grid is not
an induced minor of the graph.
-/

namespace Lax762056.Grid

open SimpleGraph InducedMinors

def squareGrid (k : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (Fin k × Fin k) :=
  (pathGraph k).boxProd (pathGraph k)

def ExcludesInducedGrid (k : ℕ) {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ¬ IsInducedMinor (squareGrid k) G

end Lax762056.Grid

concepts.title: The independence number records the maximum cut
concepts.description:
For every finite simple graph $F$,
$\alpha(G_F)=\operatorname{MaxCut}(F)+b(F)$.
An independent set chooses at most one side in each column and so determines
a cut of $F$ (empty columns may be assigned either side). The two rows for
an edge $uv$ contribute at most $2(v-u)+1$ vertices, and at most $2(v-u)$
when its endpoints lie on the same side. Conversely, every cut realizes
the sum of these bounds.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax762056.Reduction

/-!
---
title: The independence number records the maximum cut
type: lemma
---
For every finite simple graph $F$,
$\alpha(G_F)=\operatorname{MaxCut}(F)+b(F)$.
An independent set chooses at most one side in each column and so determines
a cut of $F$ (empty columns may be assigned either side). The two rows for
an edge $uv$ contribute at most $2(v-u)+1$ vertices, and at most $2(v-u)$
when its endpoints lie on the same side. Conversely, every cut realizes
the sum of these bounds.
-/

namespace Lax762056.IndependenceIdentity

open Reduction MaxCut

axiom independence_eq_maxCut_offset {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) :
  (reductionGraph F).indepNum = maxCut F + offset F

end Lax762056.IndependenceIdentity

concepts.title: Independent Set without a 5×5 induced grid minor
concepts.description:
Deciding whether a graph has an independent set of size at least $k$ is
NP-hard even when the graph excludes the $5\times5$ grid as an induced minor.
Consequently, Maximum Independent Set is NP-hard on this class.

concepts.title: Induced minors
concepts.description:
A graph $H$ is an induced minor of $G$ if its vertices have pairwise disjoint,
nonempty connected branch sets in $G$, and two distinct branch sets are joined
by an edge exactly when their vertices are adjacent in $H$. Thus edges between
retained branch sets cannot be deleted. For finite graphs this is the usual
definition by vertex deletions and edge contractions.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Connectivity.Connected

/-!
---
title: Induced minors
type: definition
---
A graph $H$ is an induced minor of $G$ if its vertices have pairwise disjoint,
nonempty connected branch sets in $G$, and two distinct branch sets are joined
by an edge exactly when their vertices are adjacent in $H$. Thus edges between
retained branch sets cannot be deleted. For finite graphs this is the usual
definition by vertex deletions and edge contractions.
-/

namespace Lax762056.InducedMinors

open SimpleGraph

structure Model {W V : Type*} (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  branch : W → Set V
  connected : ∀ v, Connected (G.induce (branch v))
  disjoint : ∀ u v, u ≠ v → Disjoint (branch u) (branch v)
  adjacent : ∀ u v, u ≠ v →
    (H.Adj u v ↔ ∃ x ∈ branch u, ∃ y ∈ branch v, G.Adj x y)

def IsInducedMinor {W V : Type*} (H : SimpleGraph W)
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (Model H G)

end Lax762056.InducedMinors

concepts.title: Maximum cuts
concepts.description:
For a graph $F$ on an ordered vertex set, each edge is represented once, by
its endpoints $u<v$. A cut is specified by a subset $S$ of vertices; its size
is the number of edges with exactly one endpoint in $S$.
$\operatorname{MaxCut}(F)$ is the largest such size, with value zero for an
edgeless graph.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax762056.GraphEncoding

/-!
---
title: Maximum cuts
type: definition
---
For a graph $F$ on an ordered vertex set, each edge is represented once, by
its endpoints $u<v$. A cut is specified by a subset $S$ of vertices; its size
is the number of edges with exactly one endpoint in $S$.
$\operatorname{MaxCut}(F)$ is the largest such size, with value zero for an
edgeless graph.
-/

namespace Lax762056.MaxCut

open Finset

noncomputable def edges {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) :
    Finset (Fin n × Fin n) := by
  classical
  exact univ.filter fun e => e.1 < e.2 ∧ F.Adj e.1 e.2

noncomputable def cutSize {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (S : Finset (Fin n)) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact ((edges F).filter fun e =>
    (e.1 ∈ S ∧ e.2 ∉ S) ∨ (e.1 ∉ S ∧ e.2 ∈ S)).card

noncomputable def maxCut {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : ℕ :=
  (univ : Finset (Fin n)).powerset.sup (cutSize F)

end Lax762056.MaxCut

concepts.title: The Bonnet–Chang reduction
concepts.description:
Order the vertices of $F$ as $0,\ldots,n-1$. For every edge $uv$ with $u<v$,
reserve rows $(uv,0)$ and $(uv,1)$ in an intermediate graph with $2n-1$
columns. Keep only columns from $2u$ through $2v$. In row $(uv,t)$ keep
only side $t$ at column $2u$ and side $1-t$ at column $2v$; keep both sides
at every intervening column. The resulting induced subgraph is $G_F$.

The additive offset is $b(F)=2\sum_{uv\in E(F),\,u<v}(v-u)$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax762056.ColumnGraph
import Lax762056.MaxCut

/-!
---
title: The Bonnet–Chang reduction
type: definition
---
Order the vertices of $F$ as $0,\ldots,n-1$. For every edge $uv$ with $u<v$,
reserve rows $(uv,0)$ and $(uv,1)$ in an intermediate graph with $2n-1$
columns. Keep only columns from $2u$ through $2v$. In row $(uv,t)$ keep
only side $t$ at column $2u$ and side $1-t$ at column $2v$; keep both sides
at every intervening column. The resulting induced subgraph is $G_F$.

The additive offset is $b(F)=2\sum_{uv\in E(F),\,u<v}(v-u)$.
-/

namespace Lax762056.Reduction

open ColumnGraph MaxCut

abbrev Edge {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) :=
  {e : Fin n × Fin n // e.1 < e.2 ∧ F.Adj e.1 e.2}

abbrev Row {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) := Edge F × Bool

abbrev Vertex {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) :=
  ColumnGraph.Vertex (Row F) (2 * n - 1)

def retainedVertices {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : Set (Vertex F) :=
  fun ((edge, tag), column, side) =>
    let u := edge.val.1.val
    let v := edge.val.2.val
    let j := column.val
    (j = 2 * u ∧ side = tag) ∨
    (2 * u < j ∧ j < 2 * v) ∨
    (j = 2 * v ∧ side = !tag)

def reductionGraph {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) :
    SimpleGraph (retainedVertices F) :=
  (columnGraph (Row F) (2 * n - 1)).induce (retainedVertices F)

noncomputable def offset {n : ℕ} (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : ℕ :=
  2 * ∑ e ∈ edges F, (e.2.val - e.1.val)

end Lax762056.Reduction

concepts.title: The reduction can be computed in polynomial time
concepts.description:
The map $(F,k)\mapsto(G_F,k+b(F))$ can be computed in polynomial time.
The output vertices may be relabeled as consecutive integers.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax762056.Reduction

/-!
---
title: The reduction can be computed in polynomial time
type: lemma
---
The map $(F,k)\mapsto(G_F,k+b(F))$ can be computed in polynomial time.
The output vertices may be relabeled as consecutive integers.
-/

namespace Lax762056.ReductionTime

open GraphEncoding Reduction

axiom reduction_polynomial_time :
  ∃ f : Instance → Instance,
    PolynomialTime f ∧
    ∀ I, Nonempty ((f I).graph ≃g reductionGraph I.graph) ∧
      (f I).threshold = I.threshold + offset I.graph

end Lax762056.ReductionTime

statements.signature:
reduction_polynomial_time : Exists fun f =>
  And (Lax762056.GraphEncoding.PolynomialTime f)
    (∀ (I : Lax762056.GraphEncoding.Instance),
      And (Nonempty ((f I).graph.Iso (Lax762056.Reduction.reductionGraph I.graph)))
        (Eq (f I).threshold (instHAdd.hAdd I.threshold (Lax762056.Reduction.offset I.graph))))

proofs.description: Apply the general obstruction to the explicit triple of cycles in the grid.

Three corner squares form an asteroidal triple, joined pairwise by paths
along the boundary of the grid.

Every independent set induces a cut, with at most the stated number of
vertices in each edge's two rows. Conversely, the explicit construction
from a maximum cut realizes the bound, including the additional vertex
for each crossing edge.

Compose the reduction from Max Cut with the graph construction. Exclusion
of the induced grid minor gives the target class. The independence-number
identity gives equivalence after shifting the threshold.

Reduce satisfiability to not-all-equal clauses, then to Max Cut. Complementary
literals are joined by an edge, and each clause contributes a triangle.
Replacing each edge occurrence by a three-edge path yields a simple
unweighted graph.

Each cycle's branch sets contain opposite sides of a column. The three
columns are distinct. The middle column is contained in the middle cycle's
closed neighborhood and separates the other two cycles, contradicting their
avoiding path.
Induced-minor exclusion passes to induced subgraphs.

Enumerate the retained vertices and their adjacency matrix, then add the
offset to the threshold. The enumeration and adjacency tests take polynomial time.
